findings.evidence: dom-1440.json: both iframes have empty text and no title or aria-label attribute recorded; focus.json stops 01-14 land on these frames with an empty name.
findings.after: <iframe id="compareIframeOff" title="Share dialog with default transitions"> and title="Share dialog with tuned transitions" on #compareIframeOn
findings.why: WCAG 2.2 4.1.2 Name, Role, Value (frames need a title, technique H64); screen-reader users hear two unnamed frames.

findings.where: Invite button focus state, inside both panes (focus/05-on.png)
findings.evidence: Focus on Invite shows only a pale grey halo (token --primary-focus-ring: rgba(0,0,0,0.3), about #b3b3b3 on white, roughly 2:1 against the white modal).
findings.why: WCAG 2.2 2.4.7 Focus Visible and 1.4.11 Non-text Contrast: the indicator needs 3:1 against the adjacent white.

findings.evidence: Screenshot shows no visible label; the only text is the placeholder "Add people" in --text-placeholder #9e9e9e on a near-white fill (about 2.6:1). Iframe DOM was not captured, so a hidden aria-label could not be confirmed.
findings.after: <label for="invite-email" class="visually-hidden">Add people by name or email</label> plus a placeholder at #676767 or darker
findings.why: WCAG 2.2 3.3.2 Labels or Instructions and 1.4.3 Contrast: a placeholder vanishes on typing and here is below 4.5:1.

findings.where: "Full access" dropdown triggers, four per dialog
findings.evidence: Every row's control reads "Full access" with a chevron; out of context a screen-reader list gives four identical "Full access" buttons with no person attached.
findings.after: <button aria-haspopup="listbox" aria-expanded="false" aria-label="Access for James Hall: Full access">
findings.why: WCAG 2.2 2.4.6 Headings and Labels and 4.1.2 Name, Role, Value: identical names for different targets, and the menu state must be exposed.

findings.evidence: dom-1440: both labels are span.compare-pane-label inside .compare-pane-heading; no heading element exists on the page, so the two regions have no navigable names.

findings.evidence: The fixed "Dark mode" toolbar button sits on the same line as "Generic AI output" and abuts its end; on scroll it stays fixed over pane content.
findings.after: At max-width 600px make .toolbar position: static (or reserve top padding equal to its height) so it never overlaps content
